doc.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: George's deathbed promise and Catholicism; Mrs. McCullum's health
summary: Before he died George asked that the children be raised Catholic and she converted; she is 76 with high blood pressure.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: No, I wasn't going to have any music. Say what you want, you're asterial. But no, he was asterial. And I asked him.
They don't have a band for Catholics.

And all the musicians come out. They always become no, no. And I didn't know. And when they got off of the... Has he been raised a Catholic too? All of the folk that night. All his people were practicing. I was also going to go to Stephen's seat. And before he died, he died. It was a promise that he made the priest to me. That he raised my children. And he did. As soon as he got seated, he told me to get the priest for me. And he told me to promise that I'd become a Catholic. My children go, Catholic, and I didn't die. I would pray all the time. I would die as happy as he didn't know I was going to die.
We're all going to go. Some of these days.
Yeah, I go some of these days. And I'm still here. I'm seven to six years old. That's a good age.
You look very healthy as well.

I got high blood pressure. I make the best of it. Some days. And rheumatism too, a wage. Some days I can get around good. And others I'd have to slow down. All you got to do is to get up by the doctor and use the old time reference. I go to the doctor when I'm there. But I disagree.
